passage: "No! My cup!" Gargi flung the blue cup across the kitchen and wailed. "It's your favourite cup, sweetie," said her mother, Parul. "Want red!" Parul held out the red one. "No red!" Gargi dropped to the floor, kicking. "You skipped your nap at Nani's, didn't you?" Parul said, sitting down beside her. "Up," Gargi sobbed, arms stretched. "Come here. No more choices, just a cuddle in the dark room." Gargi's head sank onto her shoulder.

qa.q: Where did Gargi skip her nap?
qa.a: At Nani's.

qa.q: What was Gargi feeling when she refused both cups?
qa.a: She felt overwhelmed and frustrated; she was so tired that even choosing a cup set off screaming and kicking.

qa.q: What worked for Parul, and why?
qa.a: She stopped offering choices and took Gargi for a cuddle in the dark room, because a worn-out toddler needs rest, not more decisions.

qa.q: How does Parul see Gargi's screaming?
qa.a: Parul sees it as tiredness from the missed nap rather than naughtiness, so she stays calm and sits down beside her.

grounding: Shows a toddler who missed a nap falling apart over a tiny choice, and a parent treating it as exhaustion rather than naughtiness.

passage: Note for Himani's parents, Tuesday. Himani didn't nap today; the room was too noisy. By afternoon she was not herself. When her block tower fell, she screamed. She held on to my leg, then lay flat on the mat and cried when I offered her shoes. She wasn't being difficult; she had nothing left. I dimmed the corner lights, sat with her on the cushion and hummed. She dozed before pickup. An early night may help. Swati (room teacher)

qa.q: What happened just before Himani screamed?
qa.a: Her block tower fell.

qa.q: What might Himani have been feeling when she held on to Swati's leg?
qa.a: She was probably feeling overwhelmed and in need of comfort, because being so tired made every small upset feel too big.

qa.q: Which of Swati's steps helped, and why?
qa.a: Dimming the lights, sitting close and humming gave a worn-out toddler a calm way to rest instead of more demands.

qa.q: What might change for Himani's parents after reading the note?
qa.a: They would know the crankiness comes from the missed nap, so they could plan an early night instead of treating her as naughty.

grounding: Illustrates a toddler who skipped a nap losing all ability to cope, with small upsets turning into screaming, clinging and collapsing.

passage: The temple fair in Wadgaon was too bright and too loud, and Jaya had not slept since morning. When her red balloon slipped from her fist, she screamed and dropped flat onto the dust, kicking. People turned to stare. Tushar crouched beside her. "The nap went missing today, na?" No scolding. He lifted her, found the shade behind the bangle stall, and rocked her with her cheek on his shoulder. Soon her fists opened, and she was asleep.

qa.q: What slipped from Jaya's fist?
qa.a: Her red balloon slipped from her fist.

qa.q: What was Jaya feeling when she dropped onto the dust?
qa.a: She was overwhelmed and angry; with no sleep since morning, losing the balloon was more than she could cope with.

qa.q: What did Tushar do that helped?
qa.a: He stayed calm, did not scold, and carried her to a quiet shady spot to rock her, which let her tired body finally sleep.

qa.q: How might the people staring read Jaya's screaming?
qa.a: They might see a naughty child, when really she was a tired toddler whose coping had run out.

grounding: Shows a toddler who missed her nap collapsing over a small loss because her tired brain has no coping left.

passage: Diego had spent his nap time in the car seat, wide awake, on the long drive back to Gothenburg. At the supermarket, Astrid handed him a banana, and it snapped in half. Diego howled as if the world had ended, then wrapped himself around her leg and would not let go. Astrid looked at the half-full cart, then at his red, wet face. She parked the cart beside the bread, carried him out to the car, and drove home. He was asleep before the second traffic light.

qa.q: Where did Diego spend his nap time?
qa.a: In the car seat, wide awake, on the long drive back to Gothenburg.

qa.q: Why did Diego howl when the banana snapped?
qa.a: He was so tired that a tiny disappointment felt huge and upsetting; he had no calm left to cope with it.

qa.q: Which choice of Astrid's worked, and why?
qa.a: Leaving the half-full cart and taking him home to sleep, because rest, not a lecture, was what his body needed.

qa.q: What might it be like for Astrid to leave the shopping behind?
qa.a: It may feel frustrating to abandon the half-full cart, but she put Diego's rest ahead of finishing the task.

grounding: Shows a toddler who missed a nap falling apart and clinging over a small upset, and a caregiver treating it as tiredness rather than naughtiness.

passage:
Monday: Guests came, and Manoj skipped his nap. By four he was screaming on the floor because his milk was in the green cup, not the blue one.
Tuesday: A wedding band played outside. No nap. He bit his sister's hand over a crayon, then sobbed into Noor's dupatta.
Thursday: Noor shut the windows, drew the curtain, and lay beside him at one. He slept two hours. At four he drank from the green cup without a word.

qa.q: What cup was Manoj's milk in on Monday?
qa.a: His milk was in the green cup, not the blue one.

qa.q: What was Manoj feeling when he sobbed into Noor's dupatta on Tuesday?
qa.a: He was worn out and distressed after the crayon fight, because once again he had missed his nap and had nothing left to cope with.

qa.q: What changed on Thursday, and why did it help?
qa.a: Noor made the room dark and quiet and lay beside him at one, so he got his nap and could cope with the green cup at four.

qa.q: How might Manoj's sister see the crayon fight?
qa.a: She was hurt and might think Manoj was just being mean, not knowing tiredness had used up his patience.

grounding: Shows a toddler's missed naps turning small frustrations into screaming, biting and sobbing, and a protected nap restoring his coping.

passage: The birthday party in the Andheri building ran right through Mohit's nap time. By five he was a different child. When his father, Deepak, handed him the blue cup instead of the red one, Mohit screamed and flung it. When a balloon popped, he dropped flat on the lobby floor, kicking. A neighbour frowned. 'So naughty!' Deepak only knelt, lifted him and carried him upstairs, drew the curtains and lay beside him. Mohit sobbed twice and was asleep within minutes.

qa.q: Which cup did Deepak hand Mohit?
qa.a: The blue cup instead of the red one.

qa.q: Why did Mohit scream over the cup?
qa.a: He was exhausted and overwhelmed after missing his nap, so a tiny frustration felt huge.

qa.q: What did Deepak do that helped?
qa.a: He did not scold; he carried Mohit to a dark, quiet room and lay beside him until he slept.

qa.q: How might the neighbour see Mohit's kicking?
qa.a: The neighbour sees naughtiness, not a tired toddler who has run out of ways to cope.

grounding: A toddler who missed his nap melts down over small things, and sleep, not discipline, is what he needs.
